edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence point in more than one direction, so no single pooled effect estimate is reliable enough to summarize cleanly.
edges.mechanism: Vitamin D signaling affects calcium handling, immune tone, renin-angiotensin activity, and skeletal muscle, but supplementation only changes those pathways meaningfully when baseline status is low. That helps explain why effects on Colorectal cancer are usually clearest in deficiency and muted in already replete adults.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link vitamin d to mixed effects on colorectal cancer in general adult. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
